records.source: לַמְנַצֵּ֬חַ לִבְנֵי־קֹ֬רַח מַשְׂכִּֽיל׃
records.gloss: For the director. Of the sons of Korah. A maskil.
pieces: For the music director. Of the sons of Korah. A maskil.

L.1: For the director: of the sons of Korah. A maskil.

R.1: For the leader of the music. By the family of Korah. A song to teach and give insight.

decisions.choice: The title is verse 1
decisions.reason: The title is part of the Hebrew text and is counted as verse 1, so the verse numbers here are one higher than in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: the director
decisions.reason: As in 4:1.

decisions.choice: maskil
decisions.reason: As in 42:1.

decisions.choice: the sons of Korah
decisions.reason: As in 42:1.

decisions.choice: a lament of the whole people
decisions.reason: The psalm is the prayer of the nation after a defeat. It recalls God's past help (verses 2-9), describes the disaster (10-17), insists that the people have been faithful (18-23) and cries for help (24-27). At times one voice speaks for all (verses 5, 7, 16).

decisions.choice: by the family of Korah; a song to teach and give insight
alternatives: of the sons of Korah; a maskil
decisions.reason: As in 42:1.

records.heading: Faithful, yet crushed: wake up, Lord

records.source: אֱלֹהִ֤ים׀בְּאָזְנֵ֬ינוּ שָׁמַ֗עְנוּ אֲבוֹתֵ֥ינוּ סִפְּרוּ־לָ֑נוּ פֹּ֥עַל פָּעַ֥לְתָּ בִֽ֝ימֵיהֶ֗ם בִּ֣ימֵי קֶֽדֶם׃
records.gloss: God, with our ears we have heard; our ancestors have recounted to us [the] work you worked in their days, in [the] days of old.
pieces: God, our own ears have heard it; our ancestors told us of the deeds {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} did when they lived, in times long past.

L.2: God, with our ears we have heard; our ancestors have recounted to us the work {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} did in their days, in the days of old.

R.2: God, we have heard the stories. Our grandparents and their parents told us what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} did for them long ago.

decisions.choice: our ancestors have recounted: the story handed down
decisions.reason: Israel was told to teach its children what God had done (78:3-4; Deuteronomy 6:20-23). The work meant is above all the gift of the land (verse 3).

decisions.choice: ancestors
decisions.reason: The word ('avot) is "fathers", meaning the earlier generations, women and men.

decisions.choice: our grandparents and their parents
decisions.reason: Readable uses everyday words for the earlier generations.

records.source: אַתָּ֤ה׀יָדְךָ֡ גּוֹיִ֣ם ה֭וֹרַשְׁתָּ וַתִּטָּעֵ֑ם תָּרַ֥ע לְ֝אֻמִּ֗ים וַֽתְּשַׁלְּחֵֽם׃
records.gloss: You, your hand, nations you dispossessed, and you planted them; you did harm to peoples, and you sent them out.
pieces: With {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} own hand {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} drove out nations and planted our ancestors in their place; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} struck down peoples and let our ancestors spread out.

L.3: You, [with] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand, drove out nations, and planted them; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} brought harm on peoples, and sent them out.

R.3: With {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} own power {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} forced other nations out of the land, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} put our people there instead. You punished those nations and let our people spread out over the land.

decisions.choice: your hand; you planted them: God's power settled Israel in the land
decisions.reason: God's hand is his power. Israel is pictured as a vine or tree he planted (80:9-12; Exodus 15:17).

decisions.choice: sent them out: let Israel spread like branches
decisions.reason: "Them" may be Israel, sending out its branches like a vine (80:12), or the peoples, sent away. The planting picture favors the first.

decisions.choice: our ancestors (B); our people (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who "them" are (m2).

records.source: כִּ֤י לֹ֪א בְחַרְבָּ֡ם יָ֥רְשׁוּ אָ֗רֶץ וּזְרוֹעָם֮ לֹא־הוֹשִׁ֪יעָ֫ה לָּ֥מוֹ כִּֽי־יְמִֽינְךָ֣ וּ֭זְרוֹעֲךָ וְא֥וֹר פָּנֶ֗יךָ כִּ֣י רְצִיתָֽם׃
records.gloss: For not by their sword did they possess [the] land, and their arm did not save them, but your right hand and your arm and [the] light of your face, for you delighted in them.
pieces: Their own swords did not win them the land; their own strength did not bring them rescue. Your right hand did it, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} arm, and the shining of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} face, because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} took delight in them.

L.4: For not by their sword did they take possession of the land, and their arm did not save them, but {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} right hand and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} arm and the light of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} face, for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} delighted in them.

R.4: Our ancestors did not win the land by fighting with swords. They were not strong enough to save themselves. You saved them by {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} power. You were with them and smiled on them, because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} loved them.

decisions.choice: right hand, arm: power in action
decisions.reason: The arm and the right hand are pictures of strength put to work (Exodus 15:6; Deuteronomy 4:34).

decisions.choice: the light of your face: your favor
decisions.reason: A shining face is a sign of favor, as in the priestly blessing (Numbers 6:25; 4:7).

decisions.choice: for you delighted in them: grace, not merit
decisions.reason: The land was a gift of God's free love, not won by Israel's strength or goodness (Deuteronomy 7:7-8; 9:4-6).

decisions.choice: You were with them and smiled on them
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture means (m2).

records.source: אַתָּה־ה֣וּא מַלְכִּ֣י אֱלֹהִ֑ים צַ֝וֵּ֗ה יְשׁוּע֥וֹת יַעֲקֹֽב׃
records.gloss: You, he [is] my King, God; command [the] victories of Jacob.
pieces: You alone are my King, God; give the order for Jacob's victories.

L.5: You {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} [are] my King, God; command victories for Jacob.

R.5: God, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are my King! Give the command, and the people of Jacob will win.

decisions.choice: You, he: you and no other
decisions.reason: The pronouns "you" and "he" together make a strong "you yourself".

decisions.choice: victories: acts of rescue
decisions.reason: The plural of the word for salvation (yeshu'ot), here victories in battle.

decisions.choice: my King, God; command
alternatives: my King and my God, who commands
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation divides the letters differently and reads "my King and my God, who commands". The meaning is close.

decisions.choice: Jacob: the people of Israel
decisions.reason: Israel is called by the name of its ancestor (14:7; 20:2).

decisions.choice: the people of
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that Jacob is the nation (m4).

records.source: בְּ֭ךָ צָרֵ֣ינוּ נְנַגֵּ֑חַ בְּ֝שִׁמְךָ֗ נָב֥וּס קָמֵֽינוּ׃
records.gloss: By you our foes we gore; by your name we trample [those who] rise against us.
pieces: Through {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} we gore our enemies like a bull; through {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name we stamp down those who attack us.

L.6: Through {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} we push down our foes; through {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name we trample those who rise up against us.

R.6: With {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} help we knock our enemies down. With {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} power we crush those who attack us.

decisions.choice: we gore: we push down like a bull with its horns
decisions.reason: The verb (naggach) is used of an ox goring (Exodus 21:28); Moses' blessing pictures Joseph goring the nations (Deuteronomy 33:17).

decisions.choice: your name: your power and presence
decisions.reason: To act in God's name is to act by his authority and strength (20:6, 8).

decisions.choice: like a bull
decisions.reason: Balanced makes the picture in the verb clear (m1).

records.source: כִּ֤י לֹ֣א בְקַשְׁתִּ֣י אֶבְטָ֑ח וְ֝חַרְבִּ֗י לֹ֣א תוֹשִׁיעֵֽנִי׃
records.gloss: For not in my bow do I trust, and my sword does not save me.
pieces: I do not rely on my own bow, and my sword cannot save me.

L.7: For not in my bow do I trust, and my sword does not save me.

R.7: I do not trust my bow and arrows. My sword cannot save me.

decisions.choice: I: one voice for the people
decisions.reason: The speaker changes from "we" to "I", perhaps the king or leader, or each worshiper speaking for all.

decisions.choice: not my bow: trust in God, not weapons
decisions.reason: This echoes verse 4: as with the ancestors, so now (20:8; 33:16-17).

records.source: כִּ֣י ה֭וֹשַׁעְתָּנוּ מִצָּרֵ֑ינוּ וּמְשַׂנְאֵ֥ינוּ הֱבִישֽׁוֹתָ׃
records.gloss: For you have saved us from our foes, and those who hate us you have put to shame.
pieces: No, it is {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} who rescued us from our enemies and put to shame those who hate us.

L.8: But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have saved us from our foes, and those who hate us {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have put to shame.

R.8: You are the one who saved us from our enemies. You made those who hate us look foolish.

decisions.choice: For: but rather
decisions.reason: After "not my sword" the word (ki) means "but": the saving was God's.

decisions.choice: put to shame: defeated and disgraced
decisions.reason: Shame is the failure of what one relied on, here the enemies' defeat.

records.source: בֵּֽ֭אלֹהִים הִלַּלְ֣נוּכָל־הַיּ֑וֹם וְשִׁמְךָ֓׀לְעוֹלָ֖ם נוֹדֶ֣ה סֶֽלָה׃
records.gloss: In God we have boasted all the day, and your name forever we will praise. Selah.
pieces: God has been our boast the whole day long, and to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name we will give praise for all time. Selah

L.9: In God we have boasted all the day, and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name we will praise forever. Selah

R.9: All day long we tell everyone how great God is. We will always praise {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name. Selah

decisions.choice: we have boasted: we have praised and gloried
decisions.reason: The verb (hillel) is the one in hallelujah; to boast in God is to praise him and rely on him, not on oneself (34:3).

decisions.choice: Selah: a word whose meaning is no longer known
alternatives: lift up (the voice or the music)
decisions.reason: Selah stands at the end of a line 71 times in the Psalms and 3 times in Habakkuk 3. It is probably a direction for singing or music, perhaps a pause or an interlude; the ancient Greek translation renders it with a word meaning "interlude". It is not part of what is said, and here it marks a break after the line.

decisions.choice: Selah, kept as it is
decisions.reason: Its meaning is unknown (see the meaning decision on Selah), so every level keeps the word rather than guess, and keeps it apart from the sentence.

records.source: אַף־זָ֭נַחְתָּ וַתַּכְלִימֵ֑נוּ וְלֹא־תֵ֝צֵ֗א בְּצִבְאוֹתֵֽינוּ׃
records.gloss: Yet you have rejected and humiliated us, and you do not go out with our armies.
pieces: Yet {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have thrown us aside and disgraced us; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do not go into battle with our troops.

L.10: Yet {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have rejected [us] and humiliated us, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do not go out with our armies.

R.10: But now {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have turned away from us and let us be shamed. You do not go with our soldiers when they fight.

decisions.choice: Yet: the turn to complaint
decisions.reason: The word ('af) marks a sharp turn: after the praise of verses 2-9 comes the present disaster.

decisions.choice: go out with our armies: lead them to battle
decisions.reason: God was pictured as marching out at the head of Israel's army (Numbers 10:35; 60:12).

decisions.choice: rejected: cast off
decisions.reason: As in 43:2 (zanach).

records.source: תְּשִׁיבֵ֣נוּ אָ֭חוֹר מִנִּי־צָ֑ר וּ֝מְשַׂנְאֵ֗ינוּ שָׁ֣סוּ לָֽמוֹ׃
records.gloss: You make us turn back from [the] foe, and those who hate us have plundered for themselves.
pieces: You made us retreat before the enemy, and those who hate us have helped themselves to our goods.

L.11: You make us turn back from the foe, and those who hate us have taken plunder for themselves.

R.11: You let our enemies chase us away. Those who hate us took everything they wanted from us.

decisions.choice: you make us turn back: God behind the defeat
decisions.reason: From here to verse 15 every verb of defeat has God as its subject. The people do not say that chance or the enemy is to blame, but bring the matter to God himself.

records.source: תִּ֭תְּנֵנוּ כְּצֹ֣אן מַאֲכָ֑ל וּ֝בַגּוֹיִ֗ם זֵרִיתָֽנוּ׃
records.gloss: You give us like sheep [for] food, and among the nations you have scattered us.
pieces: You hand us over like sheep to be eaten, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have spread us out among the nations.

L.12: You give us [up] like sheep [to be] eaten, and among the nations {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have scattered us.

R.12: You have let us be killed like sheep for meat. You have scattered us among other nations.

decisions.choice: like sheep for food: helpless before the slaughterer
decisions.reason: Sheep raised for meat cannot defend themselves (compare verse 23).

decisions.choice: scattered among the nations: captives taken away
decisions.reason: Prisoners of war were carried off and sold (Deuteronomy 28:64-68). The verse does not say which defeat is meant.

records.source: תִּמְכֹּֽר־עַמְּךָ֥ בְלֹא־ה֑וֹן וְלֹ֥א־רִ֝בִּ֗יתָ בִּמְחִירֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: You sell your people for no wealth, and you have not made [yourself] great by their price.
pieces: You sell off {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} own people for next to nothing; their price has not made {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} any richer.

L.13: You sell {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people for no wealth, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have not grown rich by their price.

R.13: You sold {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} own people as if they were worth nothing. You did not even ask a good price for them.

decisions.choice: you sell your people: you hand them over to enemies
decisions.reason: To sell a people is to give them into enemy hands (Judges 2:14; Deuteronomy 32:30). Here it seems God has done it for nothing, as if they were worthless to him.

decisions.choice: you have not made great by their price: you gained nothing
decisions.reason: The words are bitter irony: the sale brought God no profit.

records.source: תְּשִׂימֵ֣נוּ חֶ֭רְפָּה לִשְׁכֵנֵ֑ינוּ לַ֥עַג וָ֝קֶ֗לֶס לִסְבִיבוֹתֵֽינוּ׃
records.gloss: You make us a reproach to our neighbors, a mockery and derision to [those] around us.
pieces: You have made us a disgrace in the eyes of our neighbors, a joke and a laughingstock to all around us.

L.14: You make us a reproach to our neighbors, a mockery and a scorn to those around us.

R.14: You have let our neighbors insult us. The people around us laugh at us and make fun of us.

decisions.choice: reproach: an object of scorn
decisions.reason: The word (cherpah) is disgrace that others heap on someone (22:7).
Psalm 79:4 says almost the same of the nations around Jerusalem.

records.source: תְּשִׂימֵ֣נוּ מָ֭שָׁל בַּגּוֹיִ֑ם מְנֽוֹד־רֹ֝֗אשׁ בַּל־אֻמִּֽים׃
records.gloss: You make us a byword among the nations, a shaking of head among the peoples.
pieces: You have turned our name into a proverb among the nations; the peoples shake their heads at us.

L.15: You make us a byword among the nations, a shaking of [the] head among the peoples.

R.15: Other nations use our name as an insult. They shake their heads at us.

decisions.choice: a byword: a saying used in scorn
decisions.reason: A mashal is a proverb; a people becomes one when its name is used as an example of ruin (Deuteronomy 28:37; 1 Kings 9:7).

decisions.choice: shaking of the head: a gesture of scorn

records.source: כָּל־הַ֭יּוֹם כְּלִמָּתִ֣י נֶגְדִּ֑י וּבֹ֖שֶׁת פָּנַ֣י כִּסָּֽתְנִי׃
records.gloss: All the day my disgrace [is] before me, and [the] shame of my face has covered me,
pieces: All day long I see my disgrace, and shame is written over my face,

L.16: All the day my disgrace [is] before me, and the shame of my face has covered me,

R.16: All day long I feel how I have been disgraced. I am so ashamed that I want to hide my face.

decisions.choice: my disgrace: one voice for the people
decisions.reason: As in verse 7, one speaker voices the shame of all.

decisions.choice: the shame of my face has covered me: I am covered in shame
decisions.reason: Shame is pictured as something that covers the face (69:8).

decisions.choice: a sentence that runs on
decisions.reason: Verse 17 gives the cause, so this verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

records.source: מִ֭קּוֹל מְחָרֵ֣ף וּמְגַדֵּ֑ף מִפְּנֵ֥י א֝וֹיֵ֗ב וּמִתְנַקֵּֽם׃
records.gloss: from [the] voice of [the] one who taunts and reviles, from [the] face of [the] enemy and avenger.
pieces: because of the voice of those who taunt and mock, because of the sight of the enemy bent on revenge.

L.17: because of the voice of the one who taunts and reviles, because of the presence of the enemy and the avenger.

R.17: I hear people insult and mock me. I see my enemies, who want to get even with me.

decisions.choice: taunts and reviles: insults against God's people
decisions.reason: To revile (giddef) is to speak with contempt, often against God himself (2 Kings 19:22).

decisions.choice: the enemy and the avenger: as in 8:3
decisions.reason: The same pair of words is used in 8:3.

records.source: כָּל־זֹ֣את בָּ֭אַתְנוּ וְלֹ֣א שְׁכַחֲנ֑וּךָ וְלֹֽא־שִׁ֝קַּ֗רְנוּ בִּבְרִיתֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: All this has come on us, and we have not forgotten you, and we have not dealt falsely with your covenant.
pieces: All this has fallen on us, yet we have not put {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} out of mind or broken faith with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} covenant.

L.18: All this has come upon us, yet we have not forgotten {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, and we have not dealt falsely with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} covenant.

R.18: All these things have happened to us. But we have not forgotten {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. We have not broken the covenant {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} made with us.

decisions.choice: we have not forgotten you: suffering that is not punishment
decisions.reason: The law warned that unfaithfulness would bring defeat (Deuteronomy 28:25). The people insist that this time they have been faithful, so they cannot understand their suffering. Like Job, they bring the question to God in prayer.

decisions.choice: covenant: the bond between God and Israel
decisions.reason: The covenant (berit) is the binding agreement God made with his people at Sinai (Exodus 24:7-8).

records.source: לֹא־נָס֣וֹג אָח֣וֹר לִבֵּ֑נוּ וַתֵּ֥ט אֲשֻׁרֵ֗ינוּ מִנִּ֥י אָרְחֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: Our heart has not turned back, and our steps have not turned aside from your path,
pieces: Our hearts have not turned away, and our feet have not wandered from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} road,

L.19: Our heart has not turned back, nor have our steps turned aside from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} path,

R.19: We have not turned away from {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} in our hearts. We have not left the path {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} showed us.

decisions.choice: our steps, your path: the way we live
decisions.reason: God's path is the life his instruction sets out (17:5; 119:105).

decisions.choice: a sentence that runs on
decisions.reason: Verse 20 goes on, "yet you have crushed us", so this verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

records.source: כִּ֣י דִ֭כִּיתָנוּ בִּמְק֣וֹם תַּנִּ֑ים וַתְּכַ֖ס עָלֵ֣ינוּ בְצַלְמָֽוֶת׃
records.gloss: that you have crushed us in a place of jackals, and covered over us with deep darkness.
pieces: yet {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have crushed us in a place where only jackals live, and wrapped us in deathly darkness.

L.20: yet {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have crushed us in a place of jackals, and covered us over with deep darkness.

R.20: Still, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have crushed us and left our land a home for wild dogs. You have covered us with darkness like death.

decisions.choice: a place of jackals: ruins
decisions.reason: Jackals live among ruins and in the wilderness (Isaiah 34:13). The word (tannim) could also be read as "sea monster".

decisions.choice: deep darkness: darkness like death
decisions.reason: The word (tsalmavet) is the darkness of 23:4, deep and deadly.

decisions.choice: left our land a home for wild dogs
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture means (m1).

records.source: אִם־שָׁ֭כַחְנוּ שֵׁ֣ם אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ וַנִּפְרֹ֥שׂ כַּ֝פֵּ֗ינוּ לְאֵ֣ל זָֽר׃
records.gloss: If we had forgotten [the] name of our God, and spread out our palms to a strange god,
pieces: Had we forgotten our God's name, or lifted our hands in prayer to a foreign god,

L.21: If we had forgotten the name of our God, or spread out our hands to a foreign god,

R.21: Suppose we had forgotten our God. Suppose we had prayed to some other god.

decisions.choice: spread out our palms: prayed
decisions.reason: Prayer was made with the hands spread out and raised (1 Kings 8:22; Exodus 9:29).

decisions.choice: forgotten the name: turned away from God
decisions.reason: To forget God's name is to stop calling on him and worshiping him (Jeremiah 23:27).

records.source: הֲלֹ֣א אֱ֭לֹהִים יַֽחֲקָר־זֹ֑את כִּֽי־ה֥וּא יֹ֝דֵ֗עַ תַּעֲלֻמ֥וֹת לֵֽב׃
records.gloss: would not God search this out? For he knows [the] secrets of [the] heart.
pieces: would not God have searched it out? For {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} knows what is hidden in the heart.

L.22: would not God search this out? For {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} knows the secrets of the heart.

R.22: God would have found out, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} knows everything we think, even our secrets.

decisions.choice: he knows the secrets of the heart: their claim is honest
decisions.reason: The people appeal to the God who sees what is hidden (139:1-4). If they had been unfaithful, he would know it; they are not hiding anything.

records.source: כִּֽי־עָ֭לֶיךָ הֹרַ֣גְנוּ כָל־הַיּ֑וֹם נֶ֝חְשַׁ֗בְנוּ כְּצֹ֣אן טִבְחָֽה׃
records.gloss: For on account of you we are killed all the day; we are counted as sheep of slaughter.
pieces: Because we belong to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, we are being killed all day long; we are looked on as sheep marked for the butcher.

L.23: Yet for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} sake we are killed all the day; we are regarded as sheep for slaughter.

R.23: It is because we follow {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} that we are being killed all the time. People treat us like sheep that are taken away to be killed.

decisions.choice: for your sake: because we are yours
decisions.reason: They suffer not for being unfaithful but because they belong to God.

decisions.choice: Romans 8:36
decisions.reason: Paul quotes this verse of the sufferings of believers, and goes on to say that nothing can separate them from the love of God in Christ (Romans 8:36-39).

decisions.choice: because we belong to you (B); because we follow you (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "for your sake" means (m1).

records.source: ע֤וּרָה׀לָ֖מָּה תִישַׁ֥ן׀אֲדֹנָ֑י הָ֝קִ֗יצָה אַל־תִּזְנַ֥ח לָנֶֽצַח׃
records.gloss: Awake! Why do you sleep, Lord? Rouse yourself! Do not reject forever.
pieces: Wake up, Lord! Why are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} sleeping? Rise from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} sleep! Do not cast us off forever!

L.24: Wake up! Why do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} sleep, Lord? Rouse {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}}! Do not reject [us] forever!

R.24: Wake up, Lord! Why are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} asleep? Get up! Do not turn away from us forever!

decisions.choice: Why do you sleep?: a bold cry, not a belief that God sleeps
decisions.reason: The psalms know that God does not sleep (121:4). The people speak as if he were asleep because he seems to do nothing (7:7; 35:23).

decisions.choice: Lord
decisions.reason: As in 40:18 ('Adonai).

decisions.choice: reject
decisions.reason: As in verse 10 (zanach).

records.source: לָֽמָּה־פָנֶ֥יךָ תַסְתִּ֑יר תִּשְׁכַּ֖ח עָנְיֵ֣נוּ וְֽלַחֲצֵֽנוּ׃
records.gloss: Why do you hide your face, forget our affliction and our oppression?
pieces: Why do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} turn {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} face away and forget how we suffer and are oppressed?

L.25: Why do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} hide {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} face, [and] forget our affliction and our oppression?

R.25: Why do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} turn away from us? Why do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} forget how much we are suffering and how badly we are treated?

decisions.choice: hide your face: withdraw your favor
decisions.reason: God's face turned toward his people is his favor (verse 4); hidden, it means he seems absent (13:2; 30:8).

decisions.choice: oppression
decisions.reason: As in 42:10 (lachats).

records.source: כִּ֤י שָׁ֣חָה לֶעָפָ֣ר נַפְשֵׁ֑נוּ דָּבְקָ֖ה לָאָ֣רֶץ בִּטְנֵֽנוּ׃
records.gloss: For our soul has sunk down to the dust; our belly clings to the ground.
pieces: We are bowed down into the dust; our bodies are pressed flat against the ground.

L.26: For our soul has sunk down to the dust; our belly clings to the ground.

R.26: We lie face down in the dirt. We cannot get up.

decisions.choice: sunk to the dust, belly to the ground: utterly brought low
decisions.reason: The picture is of people lying flat in defeat and mourning, near to death (119:25).

decisions.choice: we
decisions.reason: Nefesh here is the whole self.

records.source: ק֭וּמָֽה עֶזְרָ֣תָה לָּ֑נוּ וּ֝פְדֵ֗נוּ לְמַ֣עַן חַסְדֶּֽךָ׃
records.gloss: Arise, [as] a help for us, and redeem us for the sake of your loyal love.
pieces: Rise up and come to our help! Set us free because of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} loyal love.

L.27: Arise, [as] a help for us, and redeem us for the sake of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} loyal love.

R.27: Get up and help us! Save us, because of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithful love.

decisions.choice: Arise: the call to God as the warrior of his people
decisions.reason: As in 3:8, an echo of Moses' cry when the ark set out (Numbers 10:35).

decisions.choice: redeem: set free, as by paying the price
decisions.reason: The verb (padah) is used of the rescue from Egypt (Deuteronomy 7:8). It answers verse 13: God sold his people for nothing; now let him buy them back.

decisions.choice: loyal love
decisions.reason: As in 40:11 (chesed). The last appeal rests not on the people's faithfulness but on God's.
